---

# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis

**Evidence source:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, ~32.7 minutes, capture start 2024-08-15 04:09:43 +0400 / 00:09:43 UTC). No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — this analysis is derived entirely from packet-level review of the pcap.

## 1. Infected / Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** (assigned via DHCP, transaction 0x29b669b8; an initial DHCP Request for 10.8.15.132 was NAK'd by the server 10.8.15.4) |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| Windows domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (DC: WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org, 10.8.15.4) |
| Logged-in user account | **plucero** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString, ticket exchanges with the domain controller) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Latrodectus** loader (behaviorally attributed — no AV/IDS signature was present in the evidence, so this is a **behavioral, not signature-confirmed**, identification).

Basis for attribution — the observed chain matches Latrodectus's documented TTPs precisely:
- Delivery via a fake-invoice/parcel-delivery themed phishing page, dropping a ZIP containing an oversized JavaScript downloader (~6.99 MB) padded with large blocks of benign scraped document text (OECD/IPCC report fragments, MPI programming-standard text, Mozilla dev-docs boilerplate) purely to inflate file size for AV evasion — a hallmark Latrodectus JS-dropper technique.
- The JS downloader uses the Windows **BITS** service (HTTP requests carrying `User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) to fetch a second-stage payload directly from a bare IP address rather than a domain — a distinctive and unusual TTP strongly associated with Latrodectus.
- The fetched payload is a 64-bit Windows PE32+ DLL.
- Post-infection, the host beacons persistently (308 requests over the remainder of the capture) to the same bare-IP C2 over plain HTTP using a legacy spoofed User-Agent (`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`), sending POST bodies of opaque encrypted binary data with a long randomized Cookie token — consistent with Latrodectus's custom encrypted C2 protocol. Most beacon attempts (305/308) received HTTP 400 responses from the C2, with only 3 returning HTTP 200.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — bare-IP C2; DLL payload staging (BITS) and ongoing HTTP beacon (POST /, GET /) for the remainder of the capture

**Malicious domains:**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 — Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — initial ZIP download, 2024-08-15 00:11:03 UTC
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent` — URL hardcoded inside the JS downloader; contacted at ~00:16:40 UTC (t=100.2s)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS-fetched DLL payload, 2024-08-15 00:12:00 UTC

**Transferred files / hashes:**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| `Invoice 876597035_003.zip` (Content-Disposition filename from server) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (JS downloader extracted from ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (second-stage payload; PE32+ DLL, x86-64) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

## 4. Infection Timeline (UTC, from capture)

1. **00:10:58** — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV requests `quote.checkfedexexp.com` and receives a ZIP (`Invoice 876597035_003.zip`) disguised as an invoice.
2. ZIP contains a padded JS downloader (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`).
3. **~00:16:40** — JS contacts `business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy` (hardcoded URL inside the script).
4. **00:12:00** — a BITS job (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` UA) retrieves a 64-bit DLL from `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`.
5. From ~00:15:00 UTC through the end of the capture (00:42:26 UTC), the host beacons continuously to `72.5.43.29:80` with encrypted POST payloads under a spoofed legacy-browser User-Agent — active Latrodectus C2 check-in.

No lateral movement, additional payload drops, or other externally-anomalous IPs were observed in the remainder of the traffic; all other external contacts resolve to legitimate Microsoft/Azure/Akamai/Cloudflare infrastructure consistent with normal Windows 10/11 and Edge browser telemetry.
